How to Close All Tabs from the Same Website in Chrome

Finished with a shopping session, a research rabbit hole or a stack of YouTube videos? You can close that website’s tabs together and leave your other websites open.

By Michael Wester, creator of TabTools · 5 min read · Updated October 9, 2026

On this page

  1. Close a website’s tabs in Chrome
  2. Close a different website from the popup
  3. Which tabs count as the same website?
  4. Close matching tabs manually in Chrome
  5. Use the same workflow in Firefox and Edge
  6. Reopen tabs or choose a smaller cleanup
All guides

Quick answer

With TabTools installed, right-click a tab from the website you want to close in Chrome’s tab bar and choose Close site tabs. This closes that website’s tabs across your normal browser windows, including the one you are on. Pinned tabs stay open unless you turn that off in Settings.

Close a website’s tabs in Chrome

The tab’s context menu gives you a shortcut directly from Chrome’s tab bar.

  1. Install TabTools from the Chrome Web Store.
  2. Find a tab from the website you want to close, such as the YouTube homepage or a search results page.
  3. Right-click that tab in Chrome’s tab bar.
  4. Choose Close site tabs. Tabs with the same website hostname close together.

In this example, three pages on youtube.com close while two Wikipedia tabs and Google stay open. You do not need to collect the YouTube tabs beside one another first.

If Close site tabs is not available in a tab’s menu, open that tab and right-click inside the webpage instead, or use the TabTools popup below.

This is useful when you have finished with the whole website. If you still need a particular page from it, keep that in mind before using the command: it includes the tab you right-click.

Close a different website from the popup

You can also choose a website without switching to one of its pages.

  1. Open TabTools from your browser’s extensions menu or toolbar.
  2. Find the website under Suggestions. Every website with open tabs is listed, the one with the most tabs first, with a mark for each tab and a count.
  3. Click the website’s row to close its tabs.

You can also type the website, which is useful in a long list. Enter its hostname, such as youtube.com, in Close by keyword (press Enter). TabTools lists the matching tabs as you type. Press Enter or click Close to close the tabs listed, or use the button on a row to close that tab alone. Enter the hostname without https:// or a page path.

A hostname typed here also covers its subdomains: google.com lists tabs on docs.google.com and mail.google.com too. A plain keyword such as shopping works differently: it lists tabs whose titles or addresses contain that word.

Which tabs count as the same website?

Clicking a website’s row, or choosing Close site tabs, matches the hostname, ignoring a leading www.. Different pages on that hostname match even when their paths or query parameters differ.

When closing example.comResult
example.com/article-oneCloses
www.example.com/article-twoCloses
shop.example.com/productStays open: a different subdomain
another-site.com/exampleStays open

Typing example.com in the popup’s field is broader: it also lists shop.example.com, and you can check the list before anything closes.

The command covers normal windows in the browser where you run it, and it includes the tab you are on. Pinned tabs stay open. To close them too, open Settings in the popup and turn off Keep pinned tabs open. Private or incognito tabs are excluded, and tabs in another browser application are not reached.

Close matching tabs manually in Chrome

For a small number of tabs, Chrome’s Tab Search provides a manual route.

  1. Open Tab Search with Ctrl + Shift + A on Windows or Linux, or Command + Shift + A on Mac.
  2. Search for the website’s name or hostname.
  3. Review the open-tab results and use the close control for each page you want to remove.

This lets you keep selected pages from the website. It also means reviewing and closing the matches individually. Google documents the search and close controls in its Chrome tabs guide.

Use the same workflow in Firefox and Edge

Firefox

Install TabTools for Firefox, then right-click a tab from the target website in the tab bar and choose Close site tabs. You can also right-click inside its webpage or choose a website from the popup’s suggestions.

Microsoft Edge

Install TabTools for Edge, then right-click a tab from the target website and choose Close site tabs if your Edge version shows it in the tab’s menu. Otherwise, open the tab and right-click inside the webpage, or enter the hostname in the popup. The matching rules and cross-window scope are the same as described above.

Reopen tabs or choose a smaller cleanup

After you close tabs through the popup, the result appears at the bottom of the popup with an Undo button for a few seconds. Undo reopens the tabs from that cleanup. It is offered only while the popup stays open, and in Chrome a cleanup that includes the tab you are on closes the popup with it. The right-click Close site tabs action does not offer Undo.

Either way, the tabs are then listed under Recently closed at the bottom of the popup, the latest first. Click a tab there to reopen it where it was. The list holds the last 25 tabs TabTools closed and is cleared when the browser closes; after that, look in your browser’s own recently closed tabs or history. Reopening a URL should not be treated as restoring unsaved form input or every detail of a page’s previous state.

If your goal is to retain one copy of each page, follow the guide to closing duplicate tabs. To keep all your pages and make them easier to scan, sort tabs by website instead.
